items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: One of the biggest Indian chiefs, Osceola

ctx.x: Just like New Orleans, right across -- Algiers is all mixed up with East Indian, Indian and French. That's why they speak all that Patois. They don't speak the real Parisian French. They speak Patois French. That's the same way down in there. All through the South -- at one time before the Emancipation Proclamation was

instituted, when they were running the slaves here and there, a lot of the Indians accepted them. One of the biggest Indian chiefs, Osceola, in -- off the (unintelligible) in Key West in Florida, the Everglades, down through there, they never conquered those Indians, but the Indians made peace with them because they knew that land better than anybody else. And a lot of the offsprings, like this guy -- we had a guitar player. He was part Seminole, the Seminole tribe down there, and this boy played trumpet from out…
